definitions.explanation: The act of moving personnel to different positions or departments within an organization, or rearranging the placement of objects.

examples.japanese: {人事|じんじ}の{配置換|はいちが}えがあった。
{来月|らいげつ}から{別|べつ}の{部署|ぶしょ}に{配置換|はいちが}えになる。
examples.english: I'm being reassigned to a different department starting next month.

examples.japanese: {効率|こうりつ}を{上|あ}げるために、オフィスの{配置換|はいちが}えを{行|おこな}うことにした。
examples.english: We decided to rearrange the office layout to improve efficiency.

notes:
Composed of {配置|はいち} (arrangement, placement) + {換|か}え (changing, replacing). Most commonly refers to personnel transfers within an organization but can also mean physically rearranging items or spaces.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人事|じんじ}{配置換|はいちが}え: personnel reshuffling
- {配置換|はいちが}えになる: to be reassigned
- {配置換|はいちが}えを{行|おこな}う: to carry out a reshuffling
- {配置換|はいちが}えを{命|めい}じられる: to be ordered to transfer

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {異動|いどう}: transfer, reassignment — the standard HR term for job transfers; {配置換|はいちが}え emphasizes the rearrangement aspect
- {転勤|てんきん}: job transfer (to different location) — implies geographic relocation; {配置換|はいちが}え can be within the same office
- {模様替|もようが}え: redecorating, rearranging — for rooms and spaces; {配置換|はいちが}え focuses on functional arrangement
